rationale: This is a plain equal-weight rank sum of two of the most heavily published anomalies (book-to-market and Sloan total accruals) with no conditioning or novel construction, so it is a rediscovery of the standard "value plus earnings-quality" composite rather than a genuine cross-theme insight.

The hard indicator gate zeroes roughly half the universe, creating a large mass point that will dominate the low-signal buckets and make the short leg an uninterpretable mixture of gated firms, negative-book firms, and genuine growth stocks, so the portfolio test cannot cleanly identify the claimed state dependence.

Embedding the accrual correction inside the book-value anchor (cash-verified equity over market cap) is a substantively different construction from an ex-post rank blend and has a coherent balance-sheet story, though the reviewer should note it decomposes exactly into B/M minus price-scaled cumulative accruals and so still shares variance with both parent anomalies.

The sign of the accrual-change leg is economically ambiguous — a falling (ib − oancf)/at can equally reflect deteriorating income as improving cash conversion — so the hypothesis of "accounting repair" is not what the expression reliably measures, and the wrapper is otherwise the same additive value-plus-accruals rank sum as the first proposal.

The rank product makes the low-signal (long) leg an incoherent mix of low-accrual value firms and high-accrual growth firms, and the premise contradicts the documented concentration of accrual mispricing in glamour/low-B/M stocks, so the negative expected sign is poorly supported by the expression's actual cross-sectional structure.

The five-year count of cash-backed earnings years is a genuinely different, noise-robust way to measure durable conservatism (closer in spirit to a persistence state than to a level accrual), but the discrete 0–5 support creates heavy rank ties and the earnings-yield leg plus five-year history requirement will strain coverage, so this is worth testing only if the persistence term is shown to add over the one-year accrual level.
